nodes.label: toml unbounded feature stays off: parser stops at a fixed nesting depth (80 levels in toml 1.2.1), so a 1 MiB file of brackets cannot exhaust the stack
nodes.rationale: The parser's own depth limit is the stack bound; turning the feature on needs a decision.

nodes.label: First argument compared whole: --help=x, -h=x, --version=x and -V=x as the first argument are unknown command
Option name is the text before the first equals sign: --help=x and -h=x after check-config print the help; --version and -V there are unknown option
--format=<bytes> and --config=<bytes> (name, equals sign and non UTF-8 bytes in one argument) are unexpected argument; 'value of --format' means the separate argument
result_cache or automatic_promotion given as an array (e.g. [false] or [true]) gives exactly one config.schema, never config.unsupported_capability
Nesting deeper than the toml parser allows (e.g. a dotted key with 81 parts) is config.syntax; for a dotted key or table header the finding has no location (line and column null)
io.permission_denied test under cfg(unix): file of mode 000; returns as passed when the process can still open it (root in the container), else checks exit 3 and exact output in both formats

Schema step rule: a structure that stands for a table accepts a table only, via a hand written Deserialize with a map-only visitor (a derive also accepts a sequence); top level may keep its derive; later slices follow the rule
nodes.rationale: A derived Deserialize reads a sequence by position, so result_cache = [false] slipped through as valid.
